name: Djam tang soup
summary: A fine river green cooked with stream fish. Bao Dak Lak says the soup is sweet from the green and nutty from the fish. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: Bao Dak Lak on 24 Jun 2013 calls rau djam tang an Êđê forest specialty.
howToEat: The article says the green grows along the Krông Ana, the Krông Knô, and the Serepok, and that it is scarcer than it was. In the six dry months it ages. In the rains it sprouts. The stem is fine and bruises easily. It is cooked with stream fish, rice-paddy fish, măng le, mushrooms, or forest meat. The article calls stream fish the best partner. A price is Check on arrival.
where: The rivers named are the Krông Ana, the Krông Knô, and the Serepok. A stall in town was not printed. Where to order the soup is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Canh djam tang — river green and stream fish
seoDescription: Djam tang, a fine river green, cooked with stream fish. Bao Dak Lak calls the soup sweet and nutty. A stall and a price are Check on arrival.
taste: Bao Dak Lak on 24 Jun 2013 says the soup is sweet from djam tang and nutty from the stream fish.
